name: North Dakota
agencyName: North Dakota Department of Transportation, Driver License Division

retake.retakeFee: Confirm any additional test fee with NDDOT

gdl.permitHoldingPeriod: 12 months if under 16; 6 months or until age 18 if 16 or older
gdl.nightCurfew: Restricted license holders may not drive from the later of sunset or 9 p.m. until 5 a.m.
gdl.passengerLimits: No statewide passenger cap under the standard GDL

requiredDocuments: Proof of identity and lawful presence (certified U.S. birth certificate or valid U.S. passport)
Proof of Social Security number (Social Security card or W-2)
Two proofs of North Dakota residency (e.g. utility bill, bank statement)
Certified proof of any legal name change, if applicable
process.realIdNotes: A REAL ID (gold star) must be applied for in person with proof of identity/lawful presence, Social Security number, and two proofs of North Dakota residency; documents must be originals or certified copies.
process.visionStandard: At least 20/40 in one eye, with or without corrective lenses

facts.moveOverRule: Move over a lane or slow down for stopped emergency, law-enforcement, tow and DOT vehicles displaying flashing lights
facts.interstateMaxSpeed: 80 mph on rural interstate highways unless otherwise posted
facts.schoolZoneSpeed: Obey the posted school-zone limit when children are present

bacAdult.display: An individual may not drive with an alcohol concentration of at least 0.08 by weight (or while under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs).

citation.label: Persons under the influence of intoxicating liquor or any other drugs or substances not to operate vehicle

bacUnder21.display: For a driver under 21, an alcohol concentration of at least 0.02 triggers administrative license sanctions.

citation.label: Administrative sanction for driving while having certain alcohol concentration

bacCommercial.display: Driving a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of at least 0.04 is prohibited and disqualifying.

citation.label: Commercial drivers - Alcohol and controlled substances

impliedConsentRefusal.display: Refusal to submit to testing revokes driving privileges for 180 days for a first refusal (two years for a second, three for a third); refusal is also a criminal offense punishable the same as driving under the influence.

citation.label: Revocation of privilege to drive motor vehicle upon refusal to submit to testing

openContainerProhibited.display: No person may drink, or have in the passenger area an open container of, alcoholic beverages while in a motor vehicle on a highway or right of way.

citation.label: Consumption or possession of alcoholic beverage in motor vehicle prohibited

conditions.detail: first offense in seven years with an alcohol concentration under 0.18

duiFirstSuspensionDays.display: Administrative suspension of 91 days for a first offense within seven years (180 days if the alcohol concentration was 0.18 or more).

citation.label: Administrative sanction for driving while having certain alcohol concentration

conditions.detail: access-controlled, paved, divided multilane interstate highways

ruralInterstateMaxMph.display: 80 mph is lawful on access-controlled, paved and divided multilane interstate highways; 75 mph is posted on some urban interstate segments.

conditions.detail: urban interstate segments posted at 75 mph

urbanInterstateMaxMph.display: Maximum posted speed limit on urban interstates is 75 mph (the statutory ceiling of 80 mph applies to interstates generally).

citation.label: IIHS maximum posted speed limits by state (July 2026)
citation.citation: IIHS, Maximum posted speed limits (North Dakota: 80 mph rural interstates, 75 mph urban interstates)

conditions.detail: business district, residence district or public park, unless a different limit is posted

residentialDefaultMph.display: 25 mph on any highway in a business district, residence district or public park unless a different speed is designated and posted by local authorities.

conditions.detail: during school recess or while children are going to or leaving school at opening or closing hours

schoolZoneMph.display: 20 mph when passing a school during recess or while children are going to or leaving school during opening or closing hours, unless local authorities post a lower speed.

basicSpeedLaw.display: An individual may not drive at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under the conditions, having regard for actual and potential hazards.

rightTurnOnRed.display: After stopping at a steady red signal, a driver may turn right (or left from a one-way street into a one-way street) unless a sign prohibits the turn.

leftTurnOnRedFromOneWay.display: A left turn on a steady red signal is permitted from a one-way street into a one-way street after stopping, unless prohibited by sign.

seatBeltEnforcement.display: Seat belt use is primary-enforcement statewide: the secondary-enforcement limitation in N.D.C.C. § 39-21-41.5 was repealed by 2023 N.D. Sess. Laws ch. 362, § 2.

citation.label: N.D.C.C. § 39-21-41.5 (Repealed by S.L. 2023, ch. 362, § 2); N.D.C.C. § 39-21-41.2 (occupant restraints)

conditions.detail: drivers under 18, instruction permit holders and restricted class D licensees

handheldPhone.display: No general handheld ban for adults; drivers under 18, instruction permit holders and minors with a restricted class D license may not use an electronic communication device while the vehicle is in motion (emergency exceptions).

citation.label: Use of an electronic communication device by minor prohibited

texting.display: No individual may operate a motor vehicle in motion while using a wireless communications device to compose, read or send an electronic message.

citation.label: Use of a wireless communications device prohibited

moveOver.display: Approaching a stationary vehicle displaying flashing lights (emergency, towing, highway maintenance or utility), a driver must move to a non-adjacent lane if possible, or otherwise slow to a reasonable and prudent speed.

citation.label: Vehicle to yield the right of way for stationary motor vehicles (see also § 39-10-26 for emergency vehicles)

headlightsRequired.display: Lighted lamps are required from sunset to sunrise and at any other time when visibility is insufficient (under 1,000 feet); North Dakota has no statutory wipers-on headlight rule.

parkFtFromHydrant.display: No stopping, standing or parking within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.

citation.label: Stopping, standing, or parking prohibited in specified places

conditions.detail: crosswalk at an intersection; parking on a crosswalk is prohibited entirely

parkFtFromCrosswalk.display: No parking on a crosswalk, or within 10 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.

citation.label: Stopping, standing, or parking prohibited in specified places

parkFtFromStopSign.display: No parking within 15 feet upon the approach to a flashing beacon, stop sign or traffic-control signal located at the side of a roadway.

citation.label: Stopping, standing, or parking prohibited in specified places

parkFtFromRailroad.display: No parking within 15 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

citation.label: Stopping, standing, or parking prohibited in specified places

pointSystem.display: The director assigns points for traffic convictions and acts against the license when points accumulate.

pointSuspension.display: The director must move to suspend the license once a driving record shows a total of 12 or more points. There is no fixed look-back window: the point total is reduced by one point for each three-month period without a recorded violation.

permitMinAgeMonths.display: A class D instruction permit may be issued to a resident who is at least 14 years old.

permitHoldingMonths.display: An applicant under 18 is not eligible for a class D license until the instruction permit has been held at least six months, or at least twelve months if the applicant is under 16.

supervisedHoursTotal.display: A minor must accumulate at least 50 hours of supervised behind-the-wheel experience in varied conditions before a restricted class D license is issued.

state.reason: North Dakota requires that the 50 supervised hours include night driving, gravel/dirt road driving, rural and urban driving and winter conditions, but sets no separate minimum number of night hours.

supervisedHoursNight.display: No specific night-hour minimum: the 50 required supervised hours must include night driving among other varied conditions.

gdlNightCurfew.display: A restricted class D licensee may not drive between the later of sunset or 9:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. unless accompanied by a licensed adult 18 or older.

state.reason: North Dakota imposes no young-passenger limit on restricted class D licensees; the only passenger restriction is that the driver may not carry more passengers than the vehicle manufacturer's suggested capacity.

gdlPassengerPhase1.display: No passenger-age restriction: a restricted class D licensee may not exceed the manufacturer’s suggested passenger capacity.

minLiability.display: Minimum liability coverage is $25,000 per person / $50,000 per accident for bodily injury and $25,000 for property damage.

crashReportThresholdUsd.display: A crash must be reported when it results in injury or death, or total property damage of $4,000 or more.
